## Design roles

Each part does a job for the person. These are the jobs, as questions the part answers.

<div class="odv-am-rolelist"><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Containment</b> What holds this?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Layering</b> What sits on top?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Hierarchy</b> What do you read first?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Readability</b> Can you read it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Emphasis</b> Where does the eye go?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Meaning</b> What state is it in?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Affordance</b> Can you act on it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Feedback</b> Did it respond?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Focus</b> Where is the keyboard?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Grouping</b> What belongs together?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Reach</b> Can you hit it?</span></div>

## How the decisions reach each part

Each part follows a chain: an answer about the product, the rule it set, the token that carries it, and the value you see. The numbers match the drawing.

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-1"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox"><img class="odv-am-asset" src="/anatomy/content-first/message-scroller/card-1.png" alt="Scroll region: 1" loading="lazy"/></span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">1</i><b>Scroll region</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="What holds this?">Containment</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you hit it?">Reach</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Shape · Which shape roles does it need? → Controls, badges and containers</div><div class="odv-am-why">Pill badges differ from controls.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Shape · What should control corners say? → Rounded</div><div class="odv-am-why">Rounded corners feel friendly.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>radius.container</code><span>→</span><code>radius</code><span class="odv-am-val">0.75rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> radius.12: Rounded corners feel friendly.</div></div></li></ul></div></section>

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-2"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox"><img class="odv-am-asset" src="/anatomy/content-first/message-scroller/card-2.png" alt="Space between messages: 2" loading="lazy"/></span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">2</i><b>Space between messages</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="What belongs together?">Grouping</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Spacing · Which spacing roles does it need? → Gaps and insets</div><div class="odv-am-why">No dense tables, so no row role.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Spacing · How dense is the layout? → Spacious</div><div class="odv-am-why">Room around the text helps reading.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For items that belong together, use space.gap.default. Don't use space.gap.tight.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Text needs air even inside a group.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>space.gap.group</code><span>→</span><code>gap</code><span class="odv-am-val">2rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> space.32</div></div></li></ul></div></section>

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-3"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox"><img class="odv-am-asset" src="/anatomy/content-first/message-scroller/card-3.png" alt="Focus ring: 3" loading="lazy"/></span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">3</i><b>Focus ring</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="Where is the keyboard?">Focus</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Accessibility · Which states get their own visible value? → Those and pressed</div><div class="odv-am-why">Pressed gets its own value for touch.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Accessibility · What contrast floor do we hold? → AA</div><div class="odv-am-why">AA contrast, with large text helping further.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For keyboard focus, use button/focus-ring at border-width.focus. Don't use removing the outline.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Keyboard users must always see where they are.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>border-width.focus</code><span>→</span><code>focus</code><span class="odv-am-val">2px</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. ## For agents

Agents get this same anatomy: every part, its roles, whether it is required, the tokens it reads and the decisions behind them.

- **From an AI agent:** call the `get_anatomy` tool on the Open DS MCP server, with this scheme and `message-scroller`.
- **From a terminal:** `npx open-ds anatomy content-first message-scroller`
